thread:
Jun Park: quick check-in after RFC-241 review: team proposed an alternative to lease-transfer + 409 flow: a shadow-apply pattern that accepts writes locally, replicates shadow write to resident region, and only commits after resident ack. pros: fewer client retries. cons: complexity + delayed durability and tricky billing. thoughts?
Lila S: interesting. shadow-apply reduces client-facing churn but moves complexity server-side. how do we surface resident consent? need explicit tenant consent flag for anything that writes outside residency.
Omar T: agree with Lila. Also need to bound shadow window. If resident ack takes long, do we expose provisional ids to clients? risk of split-write if resident rejects.
Priya N: from ops/runbook POV this seems riskier. prefer deterministic state transitions (transfer handshake). but OK if we can prove bounded tail. what are SLA targets for commit latency under shadow scheme?
Jun Park: proposed limits: shadow-apply commit should be <=500ms p95 in normal conditions, <=5s under transient inter-region network hiccup. if >5s, fall back to explicit transfer mode.
Ben C: implementation sketch: write arrives at region A -> A returns 202 Accepted + provisional_id -> background replicator pushes shadow to region B -> B validates policy & responds -> A upgrades provisional_id to committed and emits event. clients poll status or receive websocket callback.
Lila S: websocket callbacks are messy for many SDKs. polling with short backoff might be fine. need to include a short-lived "resident-claim" token in the write response so clients can surface friendly UX.
Omar T: what about billing semantics? tokenized provisional writes could be reaped if never confirmed. we need to bill only for committed tokens; but charging for provisional compute might be confusing. add metric: provisional_write_count and provisional_to_committed_ratio.
Priya N: security question: if resident region rejects due to compliance (e.g., PII), how does rollback look? A should emit a reversal event and mark tenant in quarantine until manual review. This needs clear console signal + CS ping.
Jun Park: agree. rollover behavior: resident reject -> mark reversal, emit audit log with resident_reject_reason, set tenant flag residency_violation=true, route reads to resident region, and notify #customer-success.
Ben C: alternative hybrid: accept short-lease with client hint for low-risk tenants, shadow-apply for medium-risk, and explicit transfer for high-risk (enterprise/legal). Tiering decided by tenant metadata at provisioning.
Lila S: tiering makes sense. need API surface to let customers pick default residency_policy and override per-route. document in billing/contract.
Omar T: we should simulate in canary cluster by replaying production traces with synthetic inter-region latency. propose toggles: USE_SHADOW=on/off, PROVISIONAL_TTL=10s, FALLBACK_THRESHOLD=5s.
Priya N: runbook additions: add steps for operator to flip USE_SHADOW, inspect provisional queue depth, force-replay entries, and how to evacuate tenants into quarantine. Include runbook checklist: create incident channel, enable verbose logging, contact legal when PII rejection occurs.
Jun Park: owners: Omar spike simulation + tooling (owner: Omar), Ben prototype provisional-id flow + metrics (owner: Ben), Lila update tenant-tiering schema + docs (owner: Lila), Priya runbook + console flags (owner: Priya). Can we get spikes this sprint?
Omar T: I can run simulation by Thu and post numbers.
Ben C: will throw prototype in a feature branch; will emit provisional metrics to a new panel.
Lila S: will add tenant metadata and a small migration job to set defaults.
Priya N: will start drafting runbook and coordinate with SRE on alert thresholds.
infra-bot: reminder: create Jira tasks with labels rfc-241, infra/shadow-apply, tenant-tiering and assign owners.
Jun Park: one more edge-case: cross-region read-after-write for clients pinned to origin region. if commit delayed, we must surface provisional state in reads until commit to avoid confusing clients. add header X-Provisional-Status in read responses.
Omar T: agree, and add metric provisional_read_hits_count. Also add privacy-safe sampling of payloads for debugging (obfuscated).
Ben C: note: SDK changes unavoidable. minimal server side-first rollout: keep server responses graceful (202 + provisional info) and add SDK opt-in in next release. older SDKs keep using transfer flow.
Lila S: ok. sounds like a plan. leaving thread open for more edge cases. :+1:
